grh_e3a752532014f6879baf.title: Stuff Of Heroes
paragraphs: Hospital handyman Hank Blevins has spent years letting his reckless brother Luke bully him and clean up after Luke's gambling debts. When Dr. Christian refuses to supply money for another rescue, Luke pressures Hank into stealing the hospital's valuable radium, arguing that no one will suspect him and that the theft will keep Luke out of jail. Hank gives in, but the theft leaves him miserable, especially after Dr. Christian explains that the radium is medically vital, registered and dangerous to anyone who mishandles it. Hank finally confronts Luke, takes the radium back and returns it to the hospital, earning a black eye in the struggle. Dr. Christian quietly lets the disappearance remain a secret and tells Hank that a man who can stand up for what is right after years of fear has the stuff that heroes are made of.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on January 17, 1940. It is listed as episode 63 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Ned LeFevre, Jerry Hausner, and Noreen Gammill. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_e353033c474d0d85d83e.title: Have A Heart
paragraphs: Nearly seventy-year-old Will Grannis has spent most of his life sheltered by his devoted sister Hattie because an illness in youth was believed to have left him with a dangerous heart condition. Dr. Christian runs a modern cardiograph and discovers that Will's heart is normal, turning what should be good news into the painful realization that decades of fear and restriction were unnecessary. Will responds not with bitterness but with a late-life revolt, traveling alone to a specialist and then across the country and beyond, spending his savings on the adventures he had always been denied. He eventually returns broke but delighted, telling Dr. Christian he packed more life into that year than many people manage in a lifetime.

grh_e3403f1e6e8dd81fdc96.title: Irene
paragraphs: Working-class Irene becomes the toast of New York society after being dressed and promoted as a fashionable young woman, while two men compete for her affection and one pays a genealogist to manufacture an aristocratic family tree. Irene's blunt Irish mother arrives and destroys the pretense, causing the snobbish suitor to withdraw. Donald Marshall values Irene rather than her pedigree and asks her to marry him, giving the Cinderella game a genuine ending.

grh_e39abdc4fd6e6fe72c40.title: The Problem of Thor Bridge
paragraphs: Grace Dunbar is accused of murdering Maria Gibson after the dead woman is found at Thor Bridge clutching a note from Grace and Grace's revolver is discovered in her wardrobe. Holmes notices damage beneath the bridge parapet and recreates the crime with Watson's revolver tied to a heavy stone. Maria Gibson killed herself and rigged the gun to be pulled into the water after firing, then planted the matching revolver in Grace's room and arranged the note so that her husband's governess would be blamed.

grh_e3ba03e00361aacc1d2d.title: The Book of Tobit
paragraphs: Holmes courts Diana Beckworth while investigating a murderer who sends warnings under the name Asmodeus. He stages a wedding, using Mycroft in disguise as the clergyman and a deliberately worthless handwritten will, to make Diana believe she has secured Holmes and his estate. grh_e312f15b7a694ee023e6.title: Soldier to Civilian
paragraphs: Using George K. Pratt's Soldier to Civilian as its guide, this dramatization follows returning veteran Ross as he discovers that coming home does not instantly restore the life he imagined overseas. His family treats him as fragile, his relationship with Christine strains under changed expectations, and difficulties finding satisfying work leave him frustrated and isolated. At a town meeting, Ross explains that veterans need useful jobs, independence, patience and ordinary common sense more than pity, parades or permanent hero treatment, framing readjustment as a problem civilians and veterans must solve together.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on May 29, 1945. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Robert Harris, Frances Heflin, Ethel Everett, Eleanor Audley, and Joseph Boland. Other credited names include Garnet Garrison as director and Rafe Blau as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.a4bc7f8ff0c42b8b|Soldier to Civilian]]. George Pratt is credited as author and Rafe Blau adapted it for radio.

grh_e3d4c9790a0690322383.title: The Rodeo Murder Mystery
paragraphs: Rocky takes an errand job with a rodeo and is quickly blamed when the show’s aging owner is murdered. The cowboys lock him in a stall to await their own rough justice, but Rocky escapes with help from an educated mule and keeps investigating. He discovers that Ringo hired a gunman to kill the old man so he could take over the financially troubled show, and the same gunman confirms the arrangement before Ringo tries to silence everyone. Rocky stops him and locates the $45,000 the owner had hidden to save the rodeo.

grh_e34f3f26fc835ae2f7cb.title: Look Who's Talking
paragraphs: Researcher Alan becomes convinced he can understand the dolphins in his laboratory, while Dr. Hughes insists their behavior is only animal response and pushes increasingly clinical experiments. One dolphin dies during Hughes's work, deepening Alan's conviction that the animals are intelligent and communicating. When Alan finally opens the way to the sea, Hughes tries to stop the escape and falls into the pool. The dolphins rescue the very man who denied their humanity and then swim away, leaving Alan with the proof of intelligence and compassion that Hughes refused to recognize.
